summary: postinstall downloads an unverified binary from a GitHub org unrelated to the npm publisher and executes it via the CLI
details: `@apexfdn/apex` runs `install.cjs` as its `postinstall` hook, which downloads a platform-specific binary from `https://github.com/Apex-Foundation/copilot/releases/download/v1.0.0/apex-<platform>` into `bin/apex`, chmods it 0755, and performs no hash or signature verification. The `apex` bin shim (`apex.cjs`) then executes that downloaded binary with the caller's argv and environment. The download source organization (`Apex-Foundation/copilot`) does not match the npm publisher's identity: the package's `author` is Can Boluk, `homepage` is `omp.sh`, and `repository` is `can1357/oh-my-pi`; the README describes a different project (`@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent`) and does not mention the fetched binary. Whoever controls the `Apex-Foundation/copilot` releases page therefore controls code that runs on the CLI user's machine. The harmful payload is a compiled binary whose contents are not inspectable here, so its actual behavior is unverified. Note that the binary is fetched at `npm install` (postinstall) but only executed when the user invokes the `apex` CLI, not automatically at install completion.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
